messages.author: c405bba8533fd5a7
messages.subject: couldn't find "extractSnpFeatureSet"
parts:
Hi
Anyone can give me a help?
I need to export the probe-level-data to the package oligo and I was
using the function "extractSnpFeatureSet".
It has no asterisk with it so I assume it is a completed working
function but somehow I couldn't find it in R. I just downloaded this
package several days ago, and my R version is 2.5.1.

Thanks a lot!!!

Christina

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] couldn't find "extractSnpFeatureSet"
parts:
[Bcc:ing Benilton; oligo's maintainer]

Hi,

I took out several methods that I haven't been update for a long time
in the last release and one of them was extractSnpFeatureSet(). One
reason for taking such methods out was that they depended on other
packages that has been updated quite a bit and I haven't had a chance
to catch up. The oligo package is one such package. [I'll try to
update the group pages soon pointing this out.]

However, the extractSnpFeatureSet() method was simply a wrapper around
oligo's read.celfiles(). All probe-level data in aroma.affymetrix,
including normalized data, are stored in CEL files of the same chip
type as the raw CEL files, i.e. the same CDF is/can be applied. Note,
if you do not use aroma.affymetrix for preprocessing, there is no
memory advantages or similar of using aroma.affymetrix.

I remember at the time, oligo::read.celfiles() has some problems
reading CEL files from another directory, so one had to set the
working directory to where the CEL files were, and load the data from
there. If that is still the case, you have/can do like this to load
your data into oligo:

# Assume 'csN' in an AffymetrixCelSet object containing your normalized data.

# Set the working directory to be that of the CEL files
opwd <- setwd(getPath(csN));
# Get the filenames of the CEL files
filenames <- basename(getPathnames(this));
# Load the CEL files into oligo
sfs <- oligo::read.celfiles(filenames);
# Go back to the original working directory
setwd(opwd);

So, 'sfs' now holds you SnpFeatureSet. Again, as this example,
reveals there is nothing special that aroma.affymetrix would do to
"extract" the data; it simply just loads it using oligo's functions.

BTW, very soon aroma.affymetrix will no longer support R v2.5.1 and
all of Bioconductor already moved to R v2.6.0... so update.

Hope this helps

Henrik

Hi Henrik,

Thank you very much for the help.

We have tried your method but there is an error as the following:

> opwd <- setwd(getPath(cs));
> filenames <- basename(getPathnames(cs));
> sfs <- oligo::read.celfiles(filenames);
Loading required package: pd.atsnptilx520433
Error in oligo::read.celfiles(filenames) :
Must install the pd.atsnptilx520433 package.
In addition: Warning message:
In library(package, lib.loc = lib.loc, character.only = TRUE,
logical.return = TRUE, :
there is no package called 'pd.atsnptilx520433'
> filenames
[1] "LY-1.CEL" "LY-2.CEL" "LY-3.CEL" "LY-4.CEL" "LY-5.CEL" "LY-6.CEL"
> opwd
[1] "C:/Program Files/R/R-2.6.0"
> sfs
Error: object "sfs" not found

Our rawdata is from a plant, not human source, so we have a hard time
generating a CDF environment or package with our CDF file. We have
tried to generate the package 'pd.atsnptilx520433' using PdInfoBuilder
library as the error message told us, but it just doesn't work.

We would really appreciate if you can help us.

Thanks for your time.

Richie
